color.$description: Semantic color contract, dark theme. Every token documents its fallback value here.

border.$description: Decorative separators only; not load-bearing for meaning.

border-strong.$description: Input borders and control outlines. 3.46:1 vs surface.

text-muted.$description: Secondary text and helper copy. 7.96:1 vs surface.

primary-text.$description: Primary-colored TEXT on the surface — ghost button labels, links. 7.09:1 vs surface, WCAG AA. `primary` itself is a surface color: on dark, violet.600 is 3.39:1 against surface, fine under white text and useless as text.

primary-fg.$description: Text and icon color on top of --sk-color-primary.

danger.$description: Destructive action surface. White text 4.72:1; 4.09:1 vs surface.

danger-fg.$description: Text and icons on the danger fill in dark theme. Cream clears 4.5:1 on the darkened danger surface.

success-fg.$description: Success text and icons on dark surfaces. On success-subtle #12291B it is 8.71:1.

warning-fg.$description: Warning text and icons on dark surfaces. On warning-subtle #2B1F0B it is 11.17:1.

success-subtle.$description: Tinted fill for badges and soft state chips. Success foreground on it is 11.01:1.

warning-subtle.$description: Tinted fill for badges and soft state chips. Warning foreground on it is 11.17:1.

danger-subtle.$description: Tinted fill for badges and soft state chips. Danger foreground on it is 9.14:1.

primary-subtle.$description: Tinted fill for badges and soft state chips. Pair it with --sk-color-primary-fg, not --sk-color-primary: white on this fill is 17.31:1, while violet is 3.04:1. Note this is the reverse of the light theme, where the pairing flips — check the theme rather than assuming.

accent-coral.$description: Decoration and data-viz accent. Never the sole carrier of state.

accent-mint.$description: Decoration and data-viz accent. Never the sole carrier of state.

focus-ring.$description: Focus indicator. 10.46:1 vs surface; 3:1 against adjacent colors.

shadow.$description: Hard offset shadow color, dark theme. Near-black rather than pure black so the shadow stays a shadow on an already-dark surface. A shadow only darkens, so it cannot meet a 3:1 ratio against a dark surface in either direction; the gate therefore applies to the light theme, and the dark theme gates the visible chrome stroke (`color.border-strong`) instead.

glass.$description: Glass overlay roles, dark theme. The only alpha values in the system; `blur` and `saturate` are theme-independent and declared in dimensions.tokens.json, every color here is per theme.

bg-strong.$description: Panels that sit over busy content and still need to carry text.

highlight.$description: Top-edge specular line; what reads as iOS rather than a translucent box.

fallback.$description: Solid surface used when `backdrop-filter` is unsupported, dark theme. Near-black rather than a light surface: a fallback must never put light text on a light panel.

shadow.$description: Per-theme colour for the layered shadow. Kept out of color.* because the ambient layer carries alpha and a colour leaf must be a resolvable hex.

hard.$description: Hard offset shadow color, dark theme. Near-black rather than pure black so the shadow stays a shadow on an already-dark surface. A shadow only darkens, so it cannot meet a 3:1 ratio against a dark surface in either direction; the gate therefore applies to the light theme, and the dark theme gates the visible chrome stroke (`color.border-strong`) instead.

ambient.$description: Ambient layer under the hard offset. Darker and stronger than light theme, because a dark surface swallows a light shadow and the hard offset alone would be invisible.
